page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare metal server featuring an Intel Xeon 2388G processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a dedicated allocation operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 3840 GB local NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU is present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core scores, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core tests and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls within the average range. While the Passmark memory score ranks in the top 10 percent, large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth benchmarks are weak, falling into the bottom 25 percent. Small-block cached memory reads, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations perform at average levels.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal configuration offers high resource density with dedicated CPU cores and a substantial 3840 GB NVMe storage allocation, avoiding the virtualization overhead of multi-tenant environments. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads. This server is well-suited for database hosting, memory-cached web serving, software compilation, and moderate-scale text processing or small-model LLM inference tasks.
